title: Night Runner Now Writes Its Own Math Model Cards | vitalii.no
description:
How a 597-line Python port of a React video component lets an overnight script generate new math lesson cards on its own, matched frame-for-frame to the real thing.

The exampleSeries card type explains a math rule in about half a minute, then walks through roughly 10 worked examples with a think-pause before each solution. It could only ever be built by hand, because the real timing and arithmetic lived inside a React/Remotion component — and the overnight generation script running on the home PC has no browser, no network, and no way to run that component at all.

I wrote a standalone Python module, using the standard library only, as a direct port of the component's token grammar and arithmetic. It uses exact fractions instead of rounded floats, and reproduces the original timing logic in the exact same operation order, down to the rounding step landing on the identical frame. A schema document and a fixtures file let the script self-check its own output against expected values, so a drift between the Python and the real component gets caught before a bad card ever reaches the render queue.

The night runner can now generate new math cards on its own, landing on frame 2992 for the approved card — not 2991.
